129:     }

142:         Self::Right(right)
143:     }

146:         requires
147:             self is Left,
148:         returns

166:         }
167:     }

170:         requires
171:             self is Left,
172:         ensures

178:         }
179:     }

181:     pub proof fn tracked_borrow_right(tracked &self) -> (tracked res: &R)
182:         requires
183:             self is Right,
184:         ensures
185:             *res == self->Right_0,
186:     {

190:         }
191:     }

252: pub ghost enum SumSP<A, B, const TOTAL: u64> {
253:     Unit,
254:     Left(Option<A>, int, bool),
255:     Right(Option<B>, int, bool),
256:     CsumInvalid,
257: }
258: 
259: impl<A, B, const TOTAL: u64> Protocol<(), Sum<A, B>> for SumSP<A, B, TOTAL> {
260:     open spec fn op(self, other: Self) -> Self {
261:         match (self, other) {
262:             (SumSP::Unit, x) => x,
263:             (x, SumSP::Unit) => x,
264:             (SumSP::Left(ov1, n1, b1), SumSP::Left(ov2, n2, b2)) => {
265:                 if !self.is_valid() || !other.is_valid() || n1 + n2 > TOTAL || b1 && b2
266:                     || ov1 is Some && ov2 is Some {
267:                     SumSP::CsumInvalid
268:                 } else {
269:                     SumSP::Left(
270:                         if ov1 is Some { ov1 } else { ov2 },
271:                         n1 + n2,
272:                         b1 || b2,
273:                     )
274:                 }
275:             },
276:             (SumSP::Right(ov1, n1, b1), SumSP::Right(ov2, n2, b2)) => {
277:                 if !self.is_valid() || !other.is_valid() || n1 + n2 > TOTAL || b1 && b2
278:                     || ov1 is Some && ov2 is Some {
279:                     SumSP::CsumInvalid
280:                 } else {
281:                     SumSP::Right(
282:                         if ov1 is Some { ov1 } else { ov2 },
283:                         n1 + n2,
284:                         b1 || b2,
285:                     )
286:                 }
287:             },
288:             _ => SumSP::CsumInvalid,
289:         }
290:     }
291: 
292:     open spec fn rel(self, s: IMap<(), Sum<A, B>>) -> bool {
293:         match self {
294:             SumSP::Unit => s.is_empty(),
295:             SumSP::Left(None, n, true) => 0 <= n <= TOTAL && s.is_empty(),
296:             SumSP::Left(Some(a), n, true) => 0 <= n <= TOTAL && s.contains_key(()) && s[()]
297:                 == Sum::<A, B>::Left(a),
298:             SumSP::Right(None, n, true) => 0 <= n <= TOTAL && s.is_empty(),
299:             SumSP::Right(Some(b), n, true) => 0 <= n <= TOTAL && s.contains_key(()) && s[()]
300:                 == Sum::<A, B>::Right(b),
301:             _ => false,
302:         }
303:     }
304: 
305:     open spec fn unit() -> Self {
306:         SumSP::Unit
307:     }
308: 
309:     proof fn commutative(a: Self, b: Self) {
310:     }
311: 
312:     proof fn associative(a: Self, b: Self, c: Self) {
313:     }
314: 
315:     proof fn op_unit(a: Self) {
316:     }
317: }
318: 
319: impl<A, B, const TOTAL: u64> SumSP<A, B, TOTAL> {
320:     pub open spec fn is_left(self) -> bool {
321:         self is Left
322:     }
323: 
324:     pub open spec fn is_right(self) -> bool {
325:         self is Right
326:     }
327: 
328:     pub open spec fn is_resource_owner(self) -> bool {
329:         match self {
330:             SumSP::Left(_, _, b) | SumSP::Right(_, _, b) => b,
331:             _ => false,
332:         }
333:     }
334: 
335:     pub open spec fn has_resource(self) -> bool {
336:         match self {
337:             SumSP::Left(ov, n, true) => ov is Some,
338:             SumSP::Right(ov, n, true) => ov is Some,
339:             _ => false,
340:         }
341:     }
342: 
343:     pub open spec fn has_no_resource(self) -> bool {
344:         match self {
345:             SumSP::Left(ov, n, true) => ov is None,
346:             SumSP::Right(ov, n, true) => ov is None,
347:             _ => false,
348:         }
349:     }
350: 
351:     pub open spec fn resource(self) -> Sum<A, B> {
352:         match self {
353:             SumSP::Left(Some(a), n, true) => Sum::Left(a),
354:             SumSP::Right(Some(b), n, true) => Sum::Right(b),
355:             _ => arbitrary(),
356:         }
357:     }
358: 
359:     pub open spec fn frac(self) -> int {
360:         match self {
361:             SumSP::Left(_, n, _) | SumSP::Right(_, n, _) => n,
362:             _ => 1,
363:         }
364:     }
365: 
366:     pub open spec fn is_valid(self) -> bool {
367:         match self {
368:             SumSP::Unit => true,
369:             SumSP::Left(ov, n, b) => 0 < n <= TOTAL && (ov is Some ==> b),
370:             SumSP::Right(ov, n, b) => 0 < n <= TOTAL && (ov is Some ==> b),
371:             _ => false,
372:         }
373:     }
374:

2602:     /// `RwLockReadGuard`s (created and ongoing creation that will succeed) represented by `read_guard_token`.

2701: struct_with_invariants! {
2702: /// Spin-based Read-write Lock
2703: ///
2704: /// # Overview
2705: ///
2706: /// This lock allows for multiple readers, or at most one writer to access
2707: /// at any point in time. The writer of this lock has exclusive access to
2708: /// modify the underlying data, while the readers are allowed shared and
2709: /// read-only access.
2710: ///
2711: /// The writing and reading portions cannot be active simultaneously, when
2712: /// one portion is in progress, the other portion will spin-wait. This is
2713: /// suitable for scenarios where the lock is expected to be held for short
2714: /// periods of time, and the overhead of context switching is higher than
2715: /// the cost of spinning.
2716: ///
2717: /// In addition to traditional read and write locks, this implementation
2718: /// provides the upgradeable read lock (`upread lock`). The `upread lock`
2719: /// can be upgraded to write locks atomically, useful in scenarios
2720: /// where a decision to write is made after reading.
2721: ///
2722: /// The type parameter `T` represents the data that this lock is protecting.
2723: /// It is necessary for `T` to satisfy [`Send`] to be shared across tasks and
2724: /// [`Sync`] to permit concurrent access via readers. The [`Deref`] method (and
2725: /// [`DerefMut`] for the writer) is implemented for the RAII guards returned
2726: /// by the locking methods, which allows for the access to the protected data
2727: /// while the lock is held.
2728: ///
2729: /// # Usage
2730: /// The lock can be used in scenarios where data needs to be read frequently
2731: /// but written to occasionally.
2732: ///
2733: /// Use `upread lock` in scenarios where related checking is performed before
2734: /// modification to effectively avoid deadlocks and improve efficiency.
2735: ///
2736: /// This lock should not be used in scenarios where lock-holding times are
2737: /// long as it can lead to CPU resource wastage due to spinning.
2738: ///
2739: /// # About Guard
2740: ///
2741: /// See the comments of [`SpinLock`].
2742: ///
2743: /// # Examples
2744: ///
2745: /// ```
2746: /// use ostd::sync::RwLock;
2747: ///
2748: /// let lock = RwLock::new(5)
2749: ///
2750: /// // many read locks can be held at once
2751: /// {
2752: ///     let r1 = lock.read();
2753: ///     let r2 = lock.read();
2754: ///     assert_eq!(*r1, 5);
2755: ///     assert_eq!(*r2, 5);
2756: ///
2757: ///     // Upgradeable read lock can share access to data with read locks
2758: ///     let r3 = lock.upread();
2759: ///     assert_eq!(*r3, 5);
2760: ///     drop(r1);
2761: ///     drop(r2);
2762: ///     // read locks are dropped at this point
2763: ///
2764: ///     // An upread lock can only be upgraded successfully after all the
2765: ///     // read locks are released, otherwise it will spin-wait.
2766: ///     let mut w1 = r3.upgrade();
2767: ///     *w1 += 1;
2768: ///     assert_eq!(*w1, 6);
2769: /// }   // upread lock are dropped at this point
2770: ///
2771: /// {
2772: ///     // Only one write lock can be held at a time
2773: ///     let mut w2 = lock.write();
2774: ///     *w2 += 1;
2775: ///     assert_eq!(*w2, 7);
2776: /// }   // write lock is dropped at this point
2777: /// ```
2778: ///
2779: /// [`SpinLock`]: super::SpinLock
2780: pub struct RwLock<T  /* : ?Sized*/ , Guard /* = PreemptDisabled*/ > {
2781:     guard: PhantomData<Guard>,

    def get_all_ghost_code(self, file):
        """Get all ghost code with their line numbers.

        Args:
            file: Path to the Verus source file

        Returns:
            List of dictionaries with ghost code information:
            [
                {
                    'type': str (e.g., 'assert', 'requires', 'ensures', etc.),
                    'start_line': int,
                    'start_column': int,
                    'end_line': int,
                    'end_column': int
                },
                ...
            ]
        """
        result = self.code_get_ghost(file)
        if result.returncode != 0:
            return []

        ghost_items = []
        # Parse output lines like: <type>:((<start_line>, <start_column>), (<end_line>, <end_column>))
        pattern = r"^([^:]+):\(\((\d+), (\d+)\), \((\d+), (\d+)\)\)$"

        for line in result.stdout.strip().split("\n"):
            if not line:
                continue
            match = re.match(pattern, line)
            if match:
                ghost_items.append(
                    {
                        "type": match.group(1),
                        "start_line": int(match.group(2)),
                        "start_column": int(match.group(3)),
                        "end_line": int(match.group(4)),
                        "end_column": int(match.group(5)),
                    }
                )

        return ghost_items


    def proof_completion_code_change_is_safe(
        self,
        origin: str,
        changed: str,
    ) -> bool:
        """
        Check if code changes are safe for proof completion.

        Ensures that no admit(), assume(), or verifier attributes are added/removed.
        Uses Lynette to verify changes don't violate safety rules.

        Args:
            origin: Original source code
            changed: Modified source code

        Returns:
            True if changes are safe, False otherwise
        """
        # Check the number of admit(), assume(, #[verifier::external_body]
        # They should not be increased
        if origin.count("admit()") != changed.count("admit()"):
            logger.error("admit() calls have been added or removed")
            return False
        if origin.count("assume(") != changed.count("assume("):
            logger.error("assume(...) calls have been added or removed")
            return False
        if origin.count("#[verifier::external_body]") != changed.count("#[verifier::external_body]"):
            logger.error("#[verifier::external_body] annotations have been added or removed")
            return False
        if origin.count("#[verifier::admit]") != changed.count("#[verifier::admit]"):
            logger.error("#[verifier::admit] annotations have been added or removed")
            return False

        with (
            tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", prefix="llm4v_orig", suffix=".rs", encoding="utf-8") as orig_f,
            tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", prefix="llm4v_changed", suffix=".rs", encoding="utf-8") as changed_f,
        ):
            orig_f.write(origin)
            orig_f.flush()
            changed_f.write(changed)
            changed_f.flush()

            m = self.run(["additions", orig_f.name, changed_f.name])

            if m.returncode == 0:
                return True
            elif m.returncode == 1:
                err_m = m.stdout.strip()
                # lynette safety check could output more information than just `Disallowed changes detected'
                if "Disallowed changes detected" in err_m:
                    logger.error("Disallowed changes detected by lynette")
                    return False
                else:
                    details = "\n".join(part for part in (m.stdout.strip(), m.stderr.strip()) if part)
                    if details.startswith("Checker error:"):
                        details = details[len("Checker error:"):].strip()
                    raise LynetteCheckerError(details or "Lynette rejected the check without a result")
            else:
                details = "\n".join(part for part in (m.stdout.strip(), m.stderr.strip()) if part)
                if details.startswith("Checker error:"):
                    details = details[len("Checker error:"):].strip()
                raise LynetteCheckerError(
                    details or f"Lynette exited with status {m.returncode}"
                )


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Check if code changes are safe for proof completion.")
    parser.add_argument("origin_file", help="Path to the original source file")
    parser.add_argument("changed_file", help="Path to the modified source file")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    try:
        with open(args.origin_file, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            origin_content = f.read()
        with open(args.changed_file, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            changed_content = f.read()
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        logger.error(f"Error reading files: {e}")
        sys.exit(1)

    lynette = Lynette()

    try:
        is_safe = lynette.proof_completion_code_change_is_safe(
            origin=origin_content,
            changed=changed_content
        )
    except LynetteCheckerError as e:
        print(f"Checker error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)

    if is_safe:
        print("Changes are safe.")
        sys.exit(0)
    else:
        print("Changes are NOT safe.")
        sys.exit(1)
